title: Henri IV to Savary de Brèves, Constantinople, 1603, BnF fr. 3541 ff. 60-104 (catalogue item 23)

plaintext.source: Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives t. VI (1853), from the Monmerqué clear copy: 18 Feb, 31 Mar, 17 Apr in full, nine as summaries; BnF fr. 4029 ff. 117v-129 holds all twelve in clear (not digitised).

transcription.source: No ciphertext in hand: fr. 3541 is not digitised. Tomokiyo's partial reading of f. 60 was the only cipher-side material.
transcription.notes: Twelve ciphered letters under one key, treated as one set. The project never had the ciphertext; the key (fr. 3462 f. 103) was transcribed in key.md.

system.summary: Homophonic figure alphabet (2-4 homophones a letter) with a nomenclator of numbers 10-99 and signs, doubles and nulls, per the key in fr. 3462 f. 103.
system.sibling_key: Key found in BnF fr. 3462 f. 103 (Tomokiyo's 'Savary de Breves' Cipher 1602-1603'); f. 104 is the different 1604 'Chiffre reformé pour Levant'.
system.notes: The key checks against Tomokiyo's partial reading of f. 60 (aussi 11, avec 12, faire 92, fault 93, a = 7/3/5).

prior_solution.where: Berger de Xivrey 1853 (from a contemporary clear copy); BnF fr. 4029 clear register copy; Tomokiyo's partial reading of f. 60

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Found the office key in BnF fr. 3462 f. 103 (Gallica canvas 109) and transcribed it; checked it against Tomokiyo's partial f. 60 reading.
Located the clear text in Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives VI: three letters in full, nine in summary; corrected Tomokiyo's f. 60 overlay.
Searched Gallica SRU, the BnF notice and Desenclos 2018 for images of fr. 3541.
BnF catalogue search found fr. 4029, a clear register copy of all twelve 1603 letters, not digitised.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Berger de Xivrey's 1853 printed texts of the three full letters (berger/*.txt) and his summaries of the other nine (berger/table_pp667-682.txt); key.md (the office key, fr. 3462 f. 103). No transcription (fr. 3541 not digitised); nine letters only as summaries.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): berger/table_pp667-682.txt is the printed table of abstracts, not the nine letters. That entry relabelled decoded, not read (summaries only); the three letters printed in full (ff. 60, 63, 66) read.

Re-read brief b25 for the nine summarised letters: BnF archivesetmanuscrits notices of fr. 4029 (cc50451m) and fr. 3541 (cc49988x) fetched, still no digitisation link; Gallica SRU returned a Cloudflare block; web search for an edition of Henri IV's letters to Breves found none. No text of the nine beyond Berger's summaries; stays decoded, not read (needs-physical-access).

outcome.texts completed on 2026-11-10 from what the folder holds: each of the four entries now carries transcription_missing, since the ciphertext (fr. 3541, not digitised) was never in hand and nothing could be transcribed. No text file was added and no new reading was made.

outcome.method_basis: The clear text comes from Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives VI (1853), printed from a contemporary clear copy (3 letters in full, 9 in summary); the office key was located in BnF fr. 3462 f. 103 and checked against Tomokiyo's partial reading of f. 60, but the fr. 3541 ciphertext is not online and was never deciphered here.
outcome.notes: Not deciphered here: the ciphertext of fr. 3541 is not online. Clear text exists in print (3 full, 9 summaries) and in fr. 4029. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the nine summarised letters relabelled decoded, not read (summaries, not texts); the three printed in full stand.

texts.transcription_missing: The project never had the ciphertext: fr. 3541 is not digitised. NOTES.md: "What stays open is the cipher text itself: fr. 3541 is not digitised, so the ciphertext of the nine summarised letters cannot be read against the key from here."
texts.summary: Henri IV to François Savary de Brèves, his ambassador at the Porte (1591-1605): among other matters, Leopold's coadjutorship obtained by the Cardinal of Lorraine without the King's knowledge, and the arms of protestants and catholics 'jà prestes d'une part et d'aultre'. Text: Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives VI (1853) pp. 31-32, printed from a contemporary clear copy (Monmerqué's 'Lettres à l'ambassadeur du Levant'); Tomokiyo's partial overlay reading of f. 60 is corrected against it in NOTES.md.
texts.note: No transcription: fr. 3541 is not digitised (project work once a reproduction is obtained).

reading_review.note: Rests on Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives VI (1853) pp. 31-32, printed from the contemporary clear copy; OCR restored to the printed words (berger/1603-02-18_reading.md). Read as sentences throughout (Ottoman disorders, Bouillon withdrawn to Germany, the King going to Metz, the Strasbourg bishopric dispute); no holes. The ciphered original fr. 3541 f. 60 is not digitised, so the reading is the print's clear text, not a decipherment made here.

reading_review.note: Rests on Berger de Xivrey VI pp. 76-78 from the contemporary clear copy (berger/1603-04-17_reading.md); read as sentences throughout (Mamoucte Bassa's conspiration, no naval request to the Porte, Spain's designs on Algiers, Elizabeth's death and James's proclamation); 5 doubtful words, all dates or one name ([?Couco]). Original fr. 3541 f. 66 not digitised: print's clear text, not a decipherment made here.

texts.summary: The nine other ciphered letters of 1603 from Henri IV to Brèves, known only from Berger de Xivrey's summaries (Lettres missives VI, pp. 667-682, Wikisource OCR).
texts.note: Summaries only, not the letters: berger/table_pp667-682.txt is Berger de Xivrey's printed table of abstracts. Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b25): no fuller text found; the BnF notices of fr. 4029 (cc50451m, the clear register ff. 118-128) and fr. 3541 (cc49988x, the ciphers) still carry no digitisation link (Gallica SRU blocked by Cloudflare from here); Guadet's supplements print none of the nine (checked 18 Sept); no modern edition of the Henri IV - Breves letters found. Stays decoded, not read; blocker needs-physical-access (a BnF reproduction of fr. 4029 ff. 117-128).

gaps.item: The nine further letters of 1603 (ff. 69-104): only Berger's summaries in the repository
gaps.detail: the full clear text is in BnF fr. 4029 ff. 118-128 and the ciphertext in fr. 3541; neither volume is digitised
